children: Palm oil rises in Asian trading thanks to bargain hunting. Weather concerns continue to support prices, with fire hotspots, haze and low water levels threatening plantation operations in Indonesia's palm-growing regions, AmInvestment Bank says in a note. Technical analysis suggests crude palm oil futures have a bearish-to-sideways bias, while declines in rival oils and crude oil may weigh on sentiment, it adds. It sees resistance at 4,960 ringgit a ton and support at 4,850 ringgit a ton. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for December delivery is up 8 ringgit at 4,906 ringgit a ton. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
